title.narrative: EMPOWERING THE INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES OF CALLE SANTA ROSA TO ENSURE THE PROTECTION OF THE GOLDEN POISON FROG RESERVE IN SOUTHWESTERN COLOMBIA.

description.narrative: The Golden Poison Frog Reserve is located in the Tumbes-Choco-Magdalena region, a world.renowned biodiversity hotspot in Colombia. Not only is it a critical habitat for the endemic and.endangered Golden Poison Frog, it also hosts a variety of other threatened species such as the Great.Currasow, Pumas and Jaguars. The perara Sia pidara indigenous community was granted the .collective ownership and autonomy to manage the Reserve and surrounding territories in 1995 However, they have never had the needed support, capacity, knowledge, or tools to protect their.territories in response to the habitat loss and degradation caused by illegal logging, gold mining, illicit.crop and agricultural encroachments, poaching and wildlife trafficking by outsiders. The purpose of.this project is to support the protection of the Reserve and its inhabitants by building the capacity of.the community to manage and protect their own forests. Specific activities include the creation of a.community-driven, protected area management plan for the Reserve; strengthening the community.ranger program; developing ecotourism practices; and conducting an analysis of alternative sources of.economic support for the community, such as payments for environmental services and sustainable.agribusiness.
